content.title: About
content.content: Grilled perch is a freshwater fish from the Percidae family, found in lakes and rivers across the Northern Hemisphere. Grilling preserves its delicate, slightly sweet flavor and yields a firm yet tender texture. Perch is often served as a main dish and can also be added to salads, pastas, and sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Perch is closely related to other members of the perch family but is distinguished by its lighter coloration and higher omega‑3 content.
In the wild, perch can grow up to 80 cm, while farmed specimens are usually smaller.
Traditionally, perch is grilled on a skillet with a small amount of oil or butter to enhance its aroma.
In some cultures, grilled perch is considered a delicacy and is served with lemon and herbs.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Grilled perch provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving delivers about 20 g of complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Perch contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The fish supplies selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, important for immunity, bone health, and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Compared with larger ocean fish, perch typically has lower mercury, making it a safer regular choice.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive grilling can create acrylamide and other potentially harmful compounds.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If seasoned with salt, monitor overall sodium intake, especially for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled perch hot with lemon, fresh herbs, and vegetable sides. It can also be sliced for salads, tossed into pasta, or used as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked perch in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months.
